title: Devotion and an empty stomach
odia:
ଠକ ଠକ ମାଳି ଭଜନ ଟାଣ
ଭୋକ କଲା ଭାତ ପାଖକୁ ଆଣ |
literal_meaning: Clack, clack go the prayer beads; sing the bhajans loud. Hunger has come—bring the rice near.
explanation: The sound of prayer beads and loud devotional singing give way to the request for rice. Outward display cannot satisfy an empty stomach: practical needs still have to be met. Neither hunger nor devotion itself is proof of hypocrisy.
meaning_odia: ତୁଳସୀ ମାଳିର ଠକଠକ ଶବ୍ଦ ଓ ଜୋରରେ ଭଜନ ଗାଇବା ପରେ ଭୋକ ଲାଗିଲେ ଭାତ ଦରକାର ହୁଏ। ବାହାରର ଭକ୍ତି ପ୍ରଦର୍ଶନରେ ପେଟ ପୂରେନାହିଁ; ମୌଳିକ ଆବଶ୍ୟକତା ପୂରଣ ପାଇଁ ପ୍ରକୃତ ବ୍ୟବସ୍ଥା ଦରକାର। ଭୋକ ଲାଗିବା ବା ଭଜନ ଗାଇବା ନିଜେ କପଟର ପ୍ରମାଣ ନୁହେଁ।
usage_example: Original imagined example: Someone makes grand declarations about living without comforts, then asks who has arranged the meal. A friend recalls that words and display do not put food on the table.
cultural_context: ମାଳି refers to tulsi prayer beads; ଠକ ଠକ gives their sound, and ଭଜନ ଟାଣ calls for loud devotional singing. The turn to rice brings the verse back to an ordinary bodily need.
